# Adobe Express Add-ons Documentation

> Official developer documentation and API reference for building Adobe Express add-ons.

Adobe Express add-ons use two primary runtime environments:

- **Add-on UI runtime:** Runs the add-on's HTML, CSS, and JavaScript user interface and provides access to browser APIs and the Add-on UI SDK.
- **Document Sandbox runtime:** Runs document-authoring code in an isolated environment and provides the Document APIs for reading and modifying Adobe Express document content.
- **Communication APIs:** Enable communication between the Add-on UI runtime and the Document Sandbox runtime.

Important terminology:

- **HTML document:** The browser DOM available through the global `document` object in the Add-on UI runtime.
- **Add-on UI SDK document:** The `addOnUISdk.app.document` API used for operations such as importing, exporting, and retrieving document information.
- **Adobe Express document:** The user's creative document, represented as a scenegraph and accessed through the Document APIs in the Document Sandbox.

Adobe Express add-ons involve three SDKs across two runtime environments:

- **Add-on UI SDK** (`addOnUISdk`, iframe/UI runtime): dialogs, OAuth, client storage, theme/locale, and document *metadata* / import / export via `addOnUISdk.app.document`.
- **Document Sandbox SDK** (`addOnSandboxSdk`, imported in `code.js`): the `runtime` object (`exposeApi()`/`apiProxy()`) used to pass data between the two runtimes. Does not itself edit document content.
- **Express Document SDK** (`express-document-sdk`, also imported in `code.js`): `editor`, `colorUtils`, `constants`, `fonts`, `viewport` — the APIs that actually read and modify the document's scenegraph.

Document APIs (Express Document SDK) only run inside the Document Sandbox (`code.js`) and can't be called from the iframe/UI runtime — use the Communication APIs to bridge between the two.

Rule of thumb: dialogs, storage, OAuth, theme/locale, import/export, document metadata → Add-on UI SDK. Creating/editing pages, shapes, text, styles → Express Document SDK inside the Document Sandbox.

The links below are organized by developer task and API runtime. Each link resolves directly to LLM-optimized Markdown.

- [Large Document Support](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/guides/learn/platform-concepts/large-document-support.md): How Adobe Express works with documents whose pages aren't all loaded at once: the active/inactive page model, the safe APIs, and the phased migration.

## Add-on UI SDK References

- [SDK Reference](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/index.md): The Adobe Express add-on SDK Reference.
- [app](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/addonsdk-app.md): Provides access to the Adobe Express host application's objects and methods to provide features such as content import and export through the document object, OAuth 2.0 authorization flows with the oauth object, theme and locale detectio...
- [currentUser](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/app-current-user.md): Provides access to the currently logged in user.
- [devFlags](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/app-dev-flags.md): This object contains flags which can be used to simulate certain behavior during development.
- [document](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/app-document.md): Provides access to the methods needed for retrieving document metadata, importing content such as images, audio and video into the document, and for exporting content from the current document.
- [oauth](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/app-oauth.md): Provides access to the OAuth API methods needed for implementing the user authorization with OAuth 2.0 use case. Be sure to check out the code samples as well for more extensive examples of using this workflow.
- [ui](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/app-ui.md): Provides you with UI related values from the Adobe Express host application where the add-on is running, so you can do things such as detect the current locale or theme in use to update your add-on user interface accordingly.
- [instance](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/addonsdk-instance.md): Represents the currently running add-on instance.
- [clientStorage](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/instance-client-storage.md): The clientStorage object provides a reference to Client Storage in the currently running add-on. Client Storage allows you to store, retrieve, and delete persistent data in the user's current browser.
- [manifest](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/instance-manifest.md): The manifest object provides access to the manifest.json file entries of the add-on.
- [runtime](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/instance-runtime.md): Represents the runtime of the current add-on.
- [dialog](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/runtime-dialog.md): Represents the modal dialog presented to the user.
- [Add-on UI SDK Constants Reference](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/addonsdk/addonsdk-constants.md): Complete technical specification for all Add-on UI SDK constants including import patterns, dual-access vs named-only exports, and detailed reference details.

## Document API References

- [Document APIs](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/index.md): An introduction to the Document APIs available in the document sandbox.
- [Classes](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/classes/editor.md): Entry point for APIs that read or modify the document's content.
- [ColorUtils](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/classes/color-utils.md): Utility methods for working with color values.
- [Node](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/classes/node.md): A Node represents an object in the scenegraph, the document's visual content tree.
- [TextContentModel](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/classes/text-content-model.md): TextContentModel is an abstract base class representing a complete piece of text content. Use this model to get or modify the text string and the style ranges applied to it.
- [VisualNode](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/classes/visual-node.md): A "node" represents an object in the scenegraph, the document's visual content tree.
- [Constants](https://developer.adobe.com/express/add-ons/docs/references/document-sandbox/document-apis/constants/overview.md): The Constants namespace groups together the enumerations used by the Document APIs.
